findings.topic: Actual crossing circle, surgery, and sign
findings.assessment: The literal identity P=A_(2,5)A_(3,5) freely reduces correctly. The stated six crossing roles give a fifth component passing over both selected strands and then under both after its cancelling fourth-strand detour. Together with the explicitly outside closing arc and cap isotopy, this supplies an actual transverse twice-punctured spanning disk, not only a peripheral group relation. The disk gives the zero longitude. The disk-twist map sends mu-q lambda to mu; the displayed augmentation action and T-squared calculation identify the local braid as 2q positive half-twists. The argument explicitly extends over the knot neighborhood, preserving its meridian. Thus q=3n gives the literal K_n, uniformly.
independent_checks: T squared equals conjugation by (ab)^(-1): passed
The literal B permutation is one four-cycle; adding the even exponent 6n preserves one component

findings.topic: Branched cover and uniform peripheral map
findings.assessment: Character zero on both the circle meridian and its longitude, using linking number two, makes its boundary split into two degree-one torus covers. Branch filling along the primitive lift of the squared knot meridian produces the actual branched-cover exterior. The two downstairs classes mu and mu+lambda form an integral basis. Their claimed signed lifts (-1,2) and (-1,1), expressed in the same raw triangulation with orientations inherited rather than independently chosen, give lambda=(0,-1) by subtraction. The resulting matrix has determinant one. Linearity therefore proves the map for every integer parameter; this is not an extrapolation from sample fillings. In particular (1,-3n) lifts to (-1,2+3n) on each circle cusp.
findings.premise_boundary: The signed raw normal-chain identities, unchanged character/gluings/cusp indices, and orientation behavior of the pinned covering routine are asserted certificate data and algorithm contracts; their arrays/source were not read.

findings.topic: Branched annulus framing and relative pants filling
findings.assessment: The double branched cover of the twice-punctured disk is an annulus. A disk-neighborhood ball with two trivial branch arcs lifts to A times I, a solid torus; its two lifted boundary circles are parallel cores. The annulus pushoff is locally the lift of the disk longitude, so it supplies the required framing with no extra integer term. Opposite orientations of the lifted cores reverse both meridian and longitude, preserving the unoriented parameter. Removing the cores gives Q times S1 with s0=s1+s2. Filling s_j+t_j f extends the product Seifert structure without exceptional fibers and leaves a solid torus with primitive outer meridian s0+(t1+t2)f. This proves the relative homeomorphism because a solid torus is determined relative to its boundary by its primitive meridian, not merely by its first homology.

findings.consequence: Lemma 4 permits the intended choice, and the definition of N and the following remaining-slope calculation both use U1 filled meridionally and U0 carrying -6n. This is a local ordering ambiguity, not a substantive failure of the argument.

The remaining exterior is therefore boundary-homeomorphic to the actual fixed outside-tangle cover. Combining the parameters into -6n on U0 and applying the fixed map gives (-1,2)+(-6n)(0,-1)=(-1,2+6n). findings.topic: Complete hyperbolic parent and genuinely embedded area-11 cusp
findings.assessment: The proof explicitly requires an existence certificate for a complete positive shape solution, including logarithmic-branch and exact equation checks. Small residual intervals alone are correctly identified as insufficient. The torus cusp link and exact oriented triangulation checks support the manifold interpretation. Face-compatible horospherical corners that stay clear of opposite faces and are disjoint along every ideal edge give an embedded cusp by assembling disjoint local corners; every pair of ideal vertices in a tetrahedron is joined by an edge. Thus the two asserted types of strict separation tests are sufficient in the geometric interpretation stated. The area-index test for two exact closed integral cycles isolates index one and establishes primitivity, while exact marking still depends separately on Section 4.
findings.premise_boundary: No complete shape intervals, standard-form scale formulae, edge-separation calculations, rational translation endpoints, or verifier source were present in the PDF for independent checking. The claims that these tests pass at area 11 and imply Re(-m+2l)>10 and 6l>19 are certificate premises of this review. The printed decimals and rejected controls are not substitutes for that certificate.

findings.status: No internal gap found conditional on stated theorem contracts
findings.topic: Every-n length bound, six theorem, and hyperbolicity
findings.assessment: The coefficient -1 makes every slope primitive. On the same fixed embedded horotorus and with l positive real, its ordinary length is at least Re(-m+2l)+n(6l)>10+19n>6 for every integer n>=0, including zero. The n>=0 restriction is used correctly. This is one linear estimate, not a finite sampling argument. Under the six-theorem contract stated in the PDF, complete finite-volume orientable N and that embedded cusp satisfy the hypotheses; neither normalized length nor a maximal cusp is substituted. The claimed irreducibility, atoroidality, non-Seifert property and infinite word-hyperbolic group exclude the nonhyperbolic geometrization alternatives. Applying geometrization then gives a closed hyperbolic filling, and the already established actual-cover identity transfers the conclusion to Sigma_2(K_n).
